subject: paper:beheshti-2020
quote: Compared to healthy controls, adults with ADHD revealed significantly higher levels of general ED (Hedges' g = 1.17, p < 0.001; Hedges' g is the adjusted effect size).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. A large meta-analytic case-control difference (13 studies, N=2,535) — among the biggest group effects in adult ADHD.

subject: paper:beheshti-2020
quote: Furthermore, symptom severity and general ED correlated significantly (r = 0.54, p < 0.001).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. ED scales with ADHD symptom severity, not just presence/absence — consistent with a dimension tied to the ADHD trait.

subject: paper:beheshti-2020
quote: Our findings support ED symptoms as a core feature of ADHD's psychopathology.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The authors' interpretation; medium because the meta-analysis could not control moderators and case-control size does not establish specificity.

subject: paper:skirrow-asherson-2013
quote: EL in adults with ADHD appears to be primarily associated with ADHD itself rather than comorbid conditions, and helps to explain some of the impairments not accounted for by classical features of the disorder.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. In comorbidity-free cases, lability is tied to ADHD itself — evidence against the 'it's just comorbid anxiety/mood' rival. Medium: small all-male sample (41 cases).

subject: paper:skirrow-asherson-2013
quote: EL was most strongly predicted by hyperactivity-impulsivity rather than subsyndromal comorbid symptoms, and contributed independently to impairment in daily life.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Lability adds to impairment over and above the classic symptoms.

subject: paper:faraone-2019-emotional-dysregulation
quote: Emotional symptoms in ADHD cause clinically significant impairments.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract of the practitioner review.

subject: paper:faraone-2019-emotional-dysregulation
quote: Although emotional symptoms are common in other psychiatric disorders, emotional impulsivity (EI), and deficient emotional self-regulation (DESR) may be sufficiently specific for ADHD to function as diagnostic criteria.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Hedged ('may be') support for EI/DESR as candidate ADHD criteria.

subject: paper:faraone-2019-emotional-dysregulation
quote: Although there is a solid theoretical rationale for considering EI and DESR to be core symptoms of ADHD, there is no consensus about how to define these constructs sin a manner that would be specific to the disorder.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract, including the source typo 'sin' (for 'in'). The specificity problem: without an ADHD-specific definition, 'core' cannot yet be operationalised — the reason the hypothesis stays being-tested.

subject: paper:moukhtarian-2017
quote: In this meta-analysis, stimulants and atomoxetine were moderately effective for EL symptoms, while effect size on core ADHD symptoms was twice as large.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Nine double-blind RCTs: SMD −0.41 on lability vs −0.8 on core symptoms.

subject: paper:moukhtarian-2017
quote: Our findings indicate that EL may be less responsive than ADHD symptoms overall, perhaps indicating the need for adjunctive psychotherapy in some cases.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The practical implication; medium because the authors note methodological issues and possible responsive/non-responsive subtypes.

subject: paper:asherson-2014-bd-bpd
quote: BD is episodic, with periods of normal mood although not necessarily function. In patients with comorbid ADHD-BD, ADHD symptoms are apparent between BD episodes.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Episodic vs trait-like time course is the key ADHD/bipolar differentiator; clinical review drawing partly on expert experience.

subject: paper:asherson-2014-bd-bpd
quote: Overlapping symptoms of BPD and ADHD include impulsivity and emotional dysregulation. Symptoms of BPD but not ADHD include frantically avoiding real/imagined abandonment, suicidal behavior, self-harm, chronic feelings of emptiness, and stress-related paranoia/severe dissociation.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Emotional dysregulation is shared with BPD; the discriminating features are BPD-specific ones.

subject: paper:asherson-2014-bd-bpd
quote: ADHD coexists in ∼20% of adults with BD or BPD.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. The differential is often 'and' — co-occurrence with the conditions that share emotional dysregulation is common.
